name: Olympus Mons
description: Tallest volcano and mountain in the Solar System (+21,229 m above Mars areoid datum; ~26 km local relief). Features a 6-caldera summit complex (72×91 km wide, 3.2 km deep), shallow 4°–5° basaltic lava flanks, and a steep basal escarpment up to 8 km tall.
source_name: USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature / NASA MGS MOLA

name: Valles Marineris
description: Immense tectonic rift canyon system extending over 4,000 km (3,761 km IAU Gazetteer length) east of the Tharsis Bulge, with troughs up to 300–600 km wide and depths reaching 7 to 11 km below the surrounding plateau. Shortlisted for Curiosity and Perseverance but rejected due to steep rugged walls.
source_name: IAU / USGS Planetary Nomenclature & NASA MGS MOLA

name: Hellas Planitia
description: Massive Noachian multi-ring impact basin in the southern highlands (~2,300 km diameter) containing the lowest elevation on Mars (-8,200 m below datum) and higher surface atmospheric column pressure.
source_name: USGS Gazetteer of Planetary Nomenclature / MGS MOLA

name: Utopia Planitia
description: Largest recognized impact basin on Mars (~3,600 km diameter) in the northern lowlands. Landing region of NASA's Viking 2 lander (1976) and CNSA's Tianwen-1 / Zhurong rover (2021), with SHARAD radar detections of subsurface scalloped ice deposits.

name: Elysium Planitia
description: Broad equatorial plain (~3,000 km diameter) south of the Elysium volcanic province, containing young Amazonian flood basalts, Cerberus Fossae tectonic fissures, and the NASA InSight geophysical lander site (4.5024°N, 135.6234°E).

name: Syrtis Major Planum
description: Hesperian low-relief basaltic shield volcano (1,200 km diameter, ~2 km high) west of Isidis Planitia. First planetary surface feature documented by Christiaan Huygens in 1659 due to its dark, dust-free basaltic albedo; hosts Meroe Patera and Nili Patera calderas.
source_name: USGS Planetary Nomenclature / Mars Global Surveyor

name: Chryse Planitia
description: Northern lowland circular plain (~1,500 km diameter) receiving catastrophic flood outflow channels (Ares, Simud, Tiu, and Kasei Valles) and hosting the historic Viking 1 (1976) and Mars Pathfinder/Sojourner (1997) landing sites.

name: Isidis Planitia
description: Giant impact basin (~1,200 km diameter) straddling the Martian crustal dichotomy boundary at 88°E. Its northwestern rim hosts Jezero Crater (Mars 2020 Perseverance) and the Nili Fossae graben system.

name: Argyre Planitia
description: Well-preserved Noachian impact basin (900 km diameter) in the southern highlands surrounded by the rugged Charitum Montes and Nereidum Montes mountain rings; exhibits the lowest kilometer-scale fractal roughness (2.036) on Mars.

name: Acidalia Planitia
description: Extensive northern lowland plain (3,400 km diameter) north of Chryse Planitia and Tempe Terra, corresponding to the classical dark albedo feature Mare Acidalium.

name: Amazonis Planitia
description: Exceptionally smooth late-Amazonian volcanic plain (2,800 km diameter) located between the Tharsis and Elysium volcanic provinces; type locality for the Amazonian geologic epoch.

name: Arcadia Planitia
description: Northern lowland volcanic plain (1,900 km diameter) northwest of Alba Mons featuring smooth Hesperian/Amazonian lava sheets and SHARAD evidence of shallow subsurface ice sheets.

name: Alba Mons
description: Immense northern Tharsis volcano (548 km central edifice, lava flow fields spanning 2,000×3,000 km, volume ~1,800×10³ km³) with an average flank slope of only 0.5° and circumferential tectonic grabens.

name: Planum Boreum
description: North polar layered plateau (1,100 km diameter) rising 2–3 km above Vastitas Borealis, capped by a permanent water-ice (H2O) mantle and dissected by the canyon Chasma Boreale.

name: Planum Australe
description: South polar layered deposit plateau (1,450 km diameter) overlain by a residual cap of CO2 and water ice; extensively probed by MRO SHARAD and Mars Express MARSIS radar.

name: Gale Crater
description: 154-km-wide Late Noachian/Early Hesperian impact crater (~3.5–3.8 Ga) containing clay and sulfate-bearing lacustrine strata, Peace Vallis alluvial fan, and the 5.5-km central peak Aeolis Mons (Mount Sharp). Explored by NASA's Curiosity rover since August 6, 2012.

name: Jezero Crater
description: 45-km-diameter impact crater on the western rim of Isidis Planitia preserving a clay- and carbonate-rich western river fan-delta, inlet/outlet valley networks (Neretva and Pliva Valles), and NASA's Mars 2020 Perseverance rover landing site.

name: Ascraeus Mons
description: Northernmost and tallest of the three Tharsis Montes shield volcanoes (460 km diameter, +18,200 m summit elevation, volume ~1,100×10³ km³) with complex internested summit calderas.

name: Pavonis Mons
description: Central shield volcano of the Tharsis Montes chain straddling the Martian equator (375 km diameter, +14,000 m peak elevation) featuring two nested summit calderas up to 5 km deep.

name: Arsia Mons
description: Southernmost Tharsis Montes shield volcano (475 km diameter, +20,000 m peak elevation, volume ~920×10³ km³) with a 130-km-wide summit caldera and extensive northwestern glacial apron deposits.

name: Elysium Mons
description: Largest volcanic edifice in the Elysium province (410 km diameter, +13,900 m peak elevation) with a 14-km-wide summit caldera and mixed basaltic lava and pyroclastic flank deposits.

name: Korolev Crater
description: 81.4-km-diameter north polar impact crater near Olympia Undae containing a permanent central mound of water ice up to 1.8 km thick and ~60 km across (~2,200 km³ of water ice).
source_name: USGS Planetary Nomenclature / Mars Express HRSC

name: Eridania Planitia
description: Southern highlands basin (600 km diameter) interpreted as the site of a large Noachian inland sea that fed the Ma'adim Vallis outflow channel toward Gusev Crater.

name: Charitum Montes
description: 850-km-long arcuate mountain belt bordering the southern rim of Argyre Planitia, exhibiting glacial cirque-like erosion and gullied massifs.

name: Libya Montes
description: 1,170-km highland mountain ring along the southern margin of the Isidis impact basin containing ancient Noachian phyllosilicate exposures.

name: Phlegra Montes
description: 1,350-km north-south chain of knobby massifs between Elysium and Amazonis Planitia surrounded by SHARAD-detected lobate debris aprons.

name: Apollinaris Mons
description: 275-km volcanic edifice (+5,000 m peak elevation) north of Gusev Crater featuring an 80-km summit caldera and extensive fan-shaped pyroclastic apron deposits.

name: Aeolis Mons (Mount Sharp)
description: 5.5-km-high layered sedimentary mountain (89 km diameter) at the center of Gale Crater recording the environmental transition from ancient clay-bearing lacustrine beds to sulfate-rich arid deposits.

name: Hecates Tholus
description: Northernmost volcano of the Elysium complex (183 km diameter, +4,700 m peak elevation) with flanks heavily dissected by channels eroded into friable volcanic ash.

name: Albor Tholus
description: Southernmost volcano of the Elysium province (170 km diameter, +4,500 m peak elevation) with a deep 30-km caldera and smooth basaltic flanks.

name: Tharsis Tholus
description: Faulted volcanic dome (158 km diameter, +9,000 m peak elevation, 7.4 km local relief) east of Ascraeus Mons exhibiting sector collapse faults.

name: Ceraunius Tholus
description: Steep volcanic cone in northern Tharsis (130 km diameter, +7,500 m peak elevation) incised by radial valleys terminating in Rahe Crater.

name: Ogygis Undae
description: Named southern hemisphere dune field (87 km extent, 1,904 km² area) outside Argyre Planitia approved by the IAU in 2015; high sand slip hazard for wheeled rovers.

name: Zunil Crater
description: Young 10.4-km rayed impact crater in Cerberus Palus imaged by MRO HiRISE showing active southeastern wall landslides and boulder-strewn ejecta.

name: Milankovič Crater
description: 114-km-diameter northern lowland crater northwest of Alba Mons imaged by THEMIS (100 m/pixel) and HRSC (50 m/pixel) with fracture-fed channelized debris flows.
